vh-5-0-4-7.title: The Weathered Pillar
vh-5-0-4-7.text:
Beside a weathered stone pillar guarding the orchard exit, you tighten your grip on the carrying poles while a lone warden whistles in the gloom. The damp air tastes of rotten leaves and cold stone, sticking to the wool of your scarf and frosting the metal rivets of the bronze Clapper cradle upon your back. Through the churning white veil, the outline of the twisted pear trees dissolves into shifting shadows that offer neither direction nor comfort.

Will you follow the thin sound of the warden's signal deeper into the haze, or turn your shoulder toward the denser thicket where the ground slopes steeply downward?
exits: Follow the warden's distant whistle into the grey haze

vh-5-0-5-0.title: The Fog-Drowned Gate
vh-5-0-5-0.text:
Standing before the fog-drowned orchard gate, you check your footing in the clinging mud while the distant guide-bells ring their hollow noon chime. The iron latch of the wicket is slick with condensation, and the heavy timber frame seems to sweat in the breath of the cloud-bank. Somewhere beyond the barrier, a mule's harness jingles faintly, swallowed instantly by the heavy moisture that hangs between earth and sky.

Do you draw back the damp bolt to continue your descent, or pause a moment longer to test the security of your pack straps?
exits: Press onward through the damp wicket

vh-5-0-5-1.title: The Timber Barrier
vh-5-0-5-1.text:
Before the heavy timber barrier lost in white mist, you listen for the warden's whistle that will tell you whether the lower path is clear. The wood is swollen with moisture, smelling sharply of wet bark and hidden earth, while the great bronze tongue on your back hums a low, sympathetic vibration against your spine. Every breath draws raw cold into your chest, reminding you of the long miles still remaining before the valley floor.

Will you lift the wooden latch and venture into the white unknown, or wait another minute for clearer signs from the guides?
exits: Press onward through the heavy mist

vh-5-0-5-2.title: The Damp Threshold
vh-5-0-5-2.text:
At the threshold of the damp orchard gate, you adjust the clapper's cradle while the surrounding fog swirls like cold smoke among the twisted boughs. Droplets gather on your eyelashes and drip steadily onto your collar, chilling your skin with the relentless damp of the upper cloud-sea. The path ahead is nothing more than a pale suggestion of mud and stone fading entirely into the grey expanse.

Do you step past the rotting gateposts into the grey gloom, or check your provisions before taking another pace?
exits: Press onward into the white orchard

vh-5-0-5-3.title: The Locked Wicket
vh-5-0-5-3.text:
Facing the locked wicket of the fog-bound orchard gate, you brace yourself against the damp chill and wait for the mandatory warden check. The iron bars are freezing to the touch, and the silence of the orchard is heavy, broken only by the distant, rhythmic drip of condensation from low-hanging branches. Your shoulders ache from the balanced weight of the bronze tongue, yearning for the moment the path opens.

Do you wait patiently for the warden to unlock the barrier, or rattle the iron latch to hurry them along?
exits: Press onward when the latch lifts

vh-5-c1.title: The Orchard Gate
vh-5-c1.text:
Deep within the choking mists of the Fogbank Orchards, the path fractures into a labyrinth of dripping boughs and treacherous mud. Those who travel with the muleBiscuit have a reliable guide whose sensitive nostrils can smell the firm soil beneath the bog, while those travelling alone must rely entirely on their own wits and the occasional faint echo of a warden's bell. The cold air bites at your fingers, and the heavy Clapper hums an anxious note against your shoulder blades as you weigh your next step.

Do you trust your faithful beast to lead the way through the blinding grey, or forge ahead on your own judgement?
exits: Biscuit knows the way through the fog
Find your own way through the fog

vh-5-1-0-0.title: The Dripping Orchards
vh-5-1-0-0.text: Drenched pear branches lean low across the muddy track, their heavy leaves weeping cold dew onto your woolen collar. You pause by a rotting larch fence, testing a moss-slick post that yields slightly to your pressure while the bronze Clapper hums a low, sympathetic vibration against your aching shoulder blades. Somewhere out in the dense white smother, a Fog-Warden blows a two-tone copper whistle, the reedy call shifting directions as the valley draft twists through the dormant trees.
exits: Follow the reedy whistle into the mist
Keep close to the rotting fence line
Pay the tax clerk and move along

vh-5-1-0-1.title: The Stone Cistern
vh-5-1-0-1.text:
Blinded by woolly mist near a stone cistern, you pause to listen for the Warden's guiding whistle ahead. The stagnant water inside the moss-choked basin ripples with tiny, invisible drops, echoing hollowly in the damp quiet. Your fingers are stiff with cold, gripping the shoulder poles so tightly your knuckles show white against the gloom.

Will you press forward into the white blur of the orchard lane, or skirt the edge of the stone cistern to find firmer footing?
exits: Step blindly into the white orchard lane
Skirt the rim of the mossy stone cistern
Listen closely for another whistle from the hidden wardens

vh-5-1-1-0.title: The Old Cider Press
vh-5-1-1-0.text: Heavy wooden beams and a massive iron screw block the sunken lane, weeping thick amber juice into the soaked mulch beneath your boots. A damp chill rises from the rotting apple pomace, clinging to your woolens as you edge around the rusted machinery. The bronze Clapper shifts in its padded cradle, its deep resonant hum answering some hidden frequency within the dripping valley walls.
exits: Climb over the slippery timbers of the press
Slip through the narrow gap near the stone wall
Wait out the chill while the cider drips

vh-5-1-1-1.title: The Empty Shed
vh-5-1-1-1.text: Frost-bitten boughs claw sharply at your sleeves as you pick your way past a boarded fruit-shed stacked with rows of empty wooden crates. The air tastes of wet cedar and cold peat, completely muffled by the heavy blanket of cloud pressing down upon the valley floor. Your boots slide slightly in the slick clay, and you lean your weight forward to keep the heavy bronze tongue balanced against your spine.
exits: Skirt the edge of the empty crates
Silence the ringing bronze with your gloved hand
Step firmly onto the firmer turf ahead
